identity.name: Nautilus Moon Phases
identity.one_liner: The asymmetric-dial Nautilus — moonphase, date, power reserve and small seconds on a 3.98mm micro-rotor caliber.

comps.condition: Steel bracelet; certificate and presentation box on record
Circa 2013; steel bracelet, certificate and boxes
Circa 2009; catalogued as new old stock, with certificate, tag and boxes

provenance_events.description: The 5712/1A brings a small-seconds, power-reserve, and date sub-dial arrangement to the steel Nautilus case. Visually busier than the 5711, the 5712/1A is preferred by collectors who want complication without paying the chronograph premium.
A 2013 5712/1A-001 in steel, blue dial, sells at the Phillips Hong Kong Watch Auction XIX for HK$640,000 (~US$82,000) on an HK$300,000-600,000 estimate.

narrative.story: Launched in 2006 alongside the 5711 for the Nautilus 30th anniversary, the 5712 kept the off-center complication layout of the 3712 it replaced: small seconds at 4-5, moonphase-date cluster at 7, power reserve under 12. The ultra-thin caliber 240 PS IRM C LU with its 22k gold micro-rotor is the reason the case stays wearable. Patek quietly dropped it from the catalogue in early 2025, ending the last steel time-and-complication Nautilus of the 5711 generation.
narrative.collector_notes: The gradient blue dial shifted tone across production years, and the asymmetric layout hides a lot of service history — check moonphase alignment and pusher feel. Tiffany-stamped examples trade in a different bracket from standard dials.
